page0.text:
It's time for the long-awaited dinner.
On the table, there's the crab egg foo young that Fuji-nee made for the three of us.
It's a simple dish where there's rice in a bowl and one serving of the omelet on top of it.
It looks like there's a yellow lid on the bowl, which doesn't really look that good.

page1.text:
But, it should make the rice taste better since it's in a bowl.
It's like a cutlet rice bowl or tempura rice bowl.
There's no way it can be bad because the topping's flavor seeps into the rice evenly.
The only downside is that the flavor would be rather mild, but it's a luxurious problem to have.

page2.text:
"Well, dig in."
"Yes, bon appétit."
"Thank you."
We all bow and start into our bowls.

page3.text:
But...
There's not an ounce of softness in the egg foo young. In fact, the strange texture is more like that of a main dish.

page4.text:
"N-NO WAY!?
We have an emergency! The crab egg foo young turned into something else...!!!"

page5.text:
"..."
...This isn't an emergency or anything.
This is more like okonomiyaki over rice.

page6.text:
"Hey, how did this happen!? I made it just like I was told!?"
"...Wow. Did your family really teach you how to make this?"

page7.text:
"Yeah. I told them I'd be making a big omelet, so they gave me flour and other stuff."
"..."

page8.text:
I wish she realized her mistake at that point.
Until now, I thought that being able to make an omelet was a basic function every human being was born with.
A crab egg foo young is only really an advanced version of an omelet.
So it was my mistake to assume that Fuji-nee couldn't mess up something like that.
That's right, Fuji-nee can't even cook an omelet...!

page9.text:
"Shirou."
...Then...
I hear a voice filled with disappointment coming from my side.
"Saber...?"
I slowly turn to her.

page10.text:
"...Shirou. This is hard to eat even for me."
...Yikes. It's hard to tell, but Saber seems mad...

page11.text:
...The nightmare of a dinner ends, and it's time for a strategy meeting.
But I've already reported to Saber about what happened today.
Since it's likely that there'll be a battle tomorrow, we might as well prepare.

page12.text:
"Then, we will not be going out tonight, Shirou?"
"...Yeah. I'm sure it's frustrating for you, but sit tight for tonight. I don't intend to fight needless battles, and more than anything, we're not in a place to be able to fight freely."

page13.text:
I'm inexperienced as a Master, and Saber has a limit to how many times she can battle since I'm not able to provide her with any magical energy.
Given our situation, it's not a good idea to be aimlessly looking around for Masters.

page14.text: "...Understood. You certainly do have a point. It is not proactive, but we do need to exercise utmost caution in order to win."

page15.text: "...However. If you have the will to fight, we must not waste any time. If we are to stay here tonight, then we should use this time to train."

page16.text:
Saber stares at me.
She doesn't even need to tell me.
I brought Saber to this dojo with that in mind.

page17.text:
"I know. Do you remember what happened last night?
We had a match since you told me that I was slacking off for coming home late... Actually, it was less of a match and more of a one-sided beatdown.
...That was a good lesson. No matter what I do, there's going to be those I can't beat. That was never more apparent than when I fought you."

page18.text:
"With that in mind, I think it's important to train with you.
I don't know how effective it'll be, but I should be able to survive a bit longer in battle if you're hard on me."

page19.text:
"Then, Shirou..."
"Yeah. Please train me whenever we have the time.
For today, that'll be until we go to bed."

page20.text:
I take the bamboo sword on the wall.
It's 8 PM.
There's still four hours until bedtime, so I'll train my heart...out...!?

page21.text:
"H-hold on, Saber!!!"
I stop Saber since I feel like my life's in danger.
Because as Saber turns to me...
"What is it? You said that you wanted to train your readiness for battle, so I am only matching your enthusiasm."
She's going to kill me.

page22.text:
"Now, let us start our training, Shirou.
First, I will knock the dullness out of your instincts. You've been slacking off. Brace yourself so that something like tonight will never happen again."
So she is mad about dinner...!

page23.text:
"W-what? That was Fuji-nee's fault!
A-and even though you complained, you ate all of it—"

page24.text:
"...There is no use in arguing.
And, Shirou? Before you lose consciousness, let me make this clear: that was out of necessity. Please do not forget that."

page26.text:
Oh man.
So I have to go through four hours of brutal torture... Grudges over food sure are scary.
